question.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{8{n}^{5}-2n}{8{n}^{4}-2}$ for $n\ge 1?$
question.worked_solution:
The dominant term in the denominator is $8{n}^{4},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{4}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{8{n}^{5}-2n}{8{n}^{4}-2} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{8{n}^{5}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{2n}{{n}^{4}})}{(\frac{8{n}^{4}}{{n}^{4}}-\frac{2}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(8n-\frac{2}{{n}^{3}})}{(8-\frac{2}{{n}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{8n-0}{8-0} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }n \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

The limit does not exist, so the sequence diverges.
